Replacing a pool with a conv gives a smaller gain than filling an empty edge, because the pool already carries a path.
Adding a conv where the direct bypass was absent gives more gain than replacing an existing op.
Replacing a skip with a conv loses the easy gradient path, so the net gain is small.
Creating the 1->2 link adds depth and a new path, which is worth more than swapping an existing op.
Pool-to-conv on the last edge gains less than none-to-conv, since the pool already passes features.
Connecting node 2 to the output with a conv unlocks the deep path.
With edge 0 gone, node 1 has no input and an edge 2 edit has nothing to carry.
Stacked convs deepen the receptive field and compose well along the 0->1->2 chain.
A conv after a skip is effectively a single conv, with less stacked-depth benefit than conv after conv.
A pooled upstream feature blurs the input, limiting what a downstream conv can extract.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 only receives through edge 2, so an edge 5 edit is worth less.
A conv feeding node 2 gives edge 5 a rich input to transform.
A skip upstream passes raw features, so a 1x1 conv on edge 5 adds little over the existing path.
A strong conv path through node 2 makes the direct conv bypass partly redundant.
With the deep path cut at edge 5, edge 3 is a main route to the output, so improving it matters more.

A skip bypass complements a conv path at node 3, adding a residual route.
A skip bypass alongside a deep conv path gives a residual benefit.
A skip is already present at node 3, so another one is redundant.
A conv on edge 4 complements an existing skip bypass, giving residual conv blocks.
Without the bypass, every route to node 3 has to be learned and the extra conv is worth less than with a skip.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 is empty and edge 4 carries nothing, so the edit is nullified.
A conv-fed node 1 gives edge 4 useful features to convolve.
With a weak pooled bypass, the conv path is the main source of learning, so it gains more.
A pool at the shared output node adds little capacity, so a conv elsewhere matters more.
A pool plus a conv at node 3 are complementary, while two convs overlap more.
A conv beside a pool at node 3 adds complementary feature types.
Pooling at node 2 from edge 1 smooths the features, so a conv on edge 2 adds less.
A pooled edge 2 adds little capacity at node 2, so a conv on edge 1 is the main contributor.
